subject: Franska
title: Adjectives and descriptions
sourceSummary: How adjectives agree in gender and number, and where adjectives are placed in a sentence.

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Mon frère est ___." (grand = tall/big)
questions.opener: "Frère" is masculine singular — the base form of the adjective.
questions.explanation: Masculine singular uses the base form: "grand".

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Mes sœurs sont ___." (sympathique = nice)
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -e (like "sympathique") don't change between masculine and feminine — only the plural is added: "sympathiques".

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "La maison est ___." (petit = small)
questions.opener: Feminine singular is usually formed with -e.

questions.prompt: Where are most descriptive adjectives placed in French?
questions.opener: Different from English, where the adjective usually comes before the noun.
questions.explanation: Most descriptive adjectives come after the noun: "une maison grande" (a big house). However, some common, short adjectives (like petit, grand, beau, joli) come BEFORE the noun.

questions.prompt: Choose the right sentence for "the black cats":
questions.explanation: "Chats" is masculine plural, so the adjective must be too: "noirs".

questions.prompt: Write the feminine singular form of "petit" (small).
Correct the error: "Mes amies sont très amusant." (My friends [female] are very funny.)
questions.opener: Check the gender and number of "amies".
steps: "Amies" is feminine plural, so the adjective "amusant" (which is masculine singular) needs to change.
Full sentence: "Mes amies sont très amusantes." (My friends are very funny.)

questions.prompt: How do French adjectives agree in gender and number, and where are they placed?
questions.opener: Adjectives "agree" with the noun they describe.
questions.answer: Basic pattern: grand/grande/grands/grandes (masculine, feminine, plural masc., plural fem.). Adjectives ending in -e (like sympathique): same form for both genders, only the plural is added. Placement: most descriptive adjectives come AFTER the noun (une maison grise), but common short adjectives like petit, grand, beau, joli, jeune, vieux, bon come BEFORE (une petite maison). Examples: chat noir (black cat), petite maison (small house), filles sympathiques (nice girls).
